100s of millions in USD are sitting in unrealized PnL, with very limited onchain liquidity.

FOMO trop uPnL traders are locked in (3,3) unwilling to sell: both to avoid nuking the tokens and because of potential reputational damage.

We're like in the air of inflated valuations and the fun can continue as long as there are new buyers and biggest holders don't sell.

Attention will expand to copy-paste the same playbook from RH to Solana (currently happening) then potentially to Arc and then other venues. Maybe Base gets their shit together.

More and more tokens are being printed and while degen limited attention gets diluted the LP pools get thinner and USD flows per token are diluted as well.

All we need is some panic in the market and FOMO top players nuke their charts one by one because, well, 'everyone was selling. How could I hold?'

Similarly LPs, who are degen farming (like me) will withdraw liquidity the moment its needed the most.

Pools will get thinner and volatility will get worse. When memecoins nuke they get less interesting to buy because PRICE is the product.

(unlike revenue tokens which get more attractive as token prices go down).

But I'm not a boomer!

The game is fun right now.

But if you are sitting on huge gains, take profits. The temptation to keep rotating them to other coins is strong.

And LPs, consider selling rewards to stablecoins instead of putting them back to the pools.

Perhaps the most and only "consequential midterm election" in the last 50 years was the 1994 Republican Revolution.  In the house the Reps  picked up 54 seats and flipped the house red for the first time since 1952.  In the senate 8 seats were picked up.  State and local elections were a red wave as well. The change was from relative control by the executive to complete and utter gridlock.  Markets fell 5% soon after the election and were choppy and down pre election. BUT this was perhaps where the phrase "Markets love Gridlock" originated.  As over the next two years 10 year interest rates fell 350 bp and SPX rallied 53%. 

Of course the Greenspan rate hike follie which brought about a fixed income massacre in 1994 and the good fortune and perhaps austerity driven surplus helped the markets it's pretty clear that gridlock was good at the time.  

This years midterms look nothing like 1994.  Gridlock is already in place and isn't going to change much AND the red response could be to break gridlock via nuclear option (though that seems remote).

So I'd personally assign higher premiums for laser companies over types of suppliers that stay in the same layer.

fundamentally it’s about culture.

it’s no longer a STRONG DEFAULT to have kids in your 20s.

it’s hard to change strong defaults, but some thoughts:

1/ government-funded influencer programs.

literally pay content creators A LOT for parenting content that gets views. it’s called “influencer” for a reason. instead feeds filled with single people doing yoga retreats in Bali at 38, you’ll see people in their 20s having fun with their kids. “I want that life”. it should be high status to have kids young.

2/ re-normalize one breadwinner per household.

achieve extreme growth in productivity via robots and AI. increase wages to the point where a family only needs one person to work. doesn’t matter if it’s the man or woman. the other stays at home and takes care of the kids. full employment is a trap.

3/ collapse the housing market.

I generally don’t believe in the idea that people don’t have kids due to finances. they just prioritize differently. however, housing is the #1 cost for most people. and it’s radically more expensive to buy today than it was 50 years ago. we need to rip of the bandaid here, and reduce dumb regulations that prevent developers from building more units. this will crash prices which will be HARD due to the strong link between mortgages and money printing. but it’s needed.

—

most governments just beat around the bush and offer incentives here and there that have no real effect.

the mindset has to be: we need to change culture.

we need to change what a 21 y/o DESIRES. and desire is memetic. if you see other people wanting something, you want that thing too. see Girard.

housing is a challenge that needs to be solved, but this is not really about finances. it’s about re-programming STRONG DEFAULTS.
